chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Mīthamī, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī al-ʿAbbās, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:
I throw at a man something the like of which does not kill. He said: “This is a mistake.”
Then he took a small pebble and threw with it.

I said: He threw at a sheep, but struck a man. He said: “This is the mistake about which there is no doubt; and deliberate killing is when he strikes with something by the like of which one is killed.”

key_terms.الشَّاةَ: the sheep, mentioned in contrast to a human target
key_terms.حَصَاةً: a small pebble used here as an example of a non-lethal object

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith distinguish accidental killing from intentional killing in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal distinction between accidental and intentional injury or killing in cases involving thrown objects. It clarifies that using something not normally lethal is classified as mistake, while deliberate harm involves striking with something of the kind that ordinarily kills.
